scenes.title: Makefiles & Task Automation
scenes.narration: A Makefile turns long, easy-to-forget commands into simple named tasks that anyone on the team can run consistently.

scenes.title: Why Data Teams Use Make
bullets: It gives common workflows short, memorable names like make test or make run.
It documents your project's key commands in one discoverable place.
It ensures everyone runs setup and pipelines exactly the same way.
scenes.narration: Make collapses complex invocations into short verbs, so make test replaces a long, error-prone command. Because every task lives in one file, the Makefile doubles as living documentation of how to operate the project. And since everyone runs the same targets, subtle differences between team members' commands simply disappear.

scenes.title: A Data Project Makefile
scenes.code:
.PHONY: install test run clean

install:
	pip install -r requirements.txt

test:
	pytest -v

run:
	python etl.py

clean:
	rm -rf __pycache__ *.pyc
scenes.narration: Each label ending in a colon is a target you invoke with make plus its name. The indented lines beneath are the shell commands that run, and they must be indented with a real tab. Declaring these names under .PHONY tells Make they are commands rather than files to build. Now install, test, run, and clean become one-word operations for the whole team.

scenes.title: Running Targets
scenes.narration: The daily rhythm becomes wonderfully simple. You run make install to set up dependencies, make test to verify everything, make run to execute the pipeline, and make clean to tidy up afterward. Four short commands cover the entire workflow.

scenes.text: Makefile recipes must be indented with real tabs, not spaces — this is the single most common Makefile mistake.
scenes.narration: Make is strict about indentation and requires actual tab characters before each command. Spaces will produce a confusing error, so watch your editor's settings.
